# Privacy notice — template for businesses using this assistant

> **How to use this template.** It is written for the business that embeds the
> assistant on its own website. That business is the **data controller**: it decides
> what the assistant is for and whose questions it answers. Complete every
> `[[FILL: ...]]` marker, keep the factual statements as they are, and publish the
> result where visitors can read it before they start a chat.
>
> The statements below describe what the software actually does. They are generated
> from the code that implements the behaviour, and a test fails if this file drifts
> from it — so do not "improve" a number or a table here; change the code instead, or
> the document becomes a claim nobody can keep.

## 1. Who is responsible for your information

[[FILL: business_legal_name]], [[FILL: business_address]], is the controller of
the personal data described here. Privacy contact: [[FILL: business_contact]].

The assistant runs on a platform operated by [[FILL: platform_legal_name]], which
processes that data on the business's behalf under a data processing agreement.

## 2. What the assistant collects

Only what a conversation needs, and only once you open the chat. Before you open it,
the assistant stores nothing on your device and creates nothing on the server.

| What | When | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Your messages to the assistant | When you send them | To answer your question |
| The assistant's answers, with the sources they were drawn from | When it answers | To show you the answer and where it came from |
| The page address you were on when the chat started | When the conversation starts | So the team knows what you were looking at |
| A random session identifier for this browser tab | When the conversation starts | To keep one conversation together; it is not a cookie and it is not used to identify you across sites |
| Your name and email address | Only if you choose to leave them to ask for a person to follow up | So the business can reply to you |
| A thumbs-up or thumbs-down, and any comment you add | Only if you rate an answer | So the business can improve its answers |
| Attachments you add, if the assistant offers that | Only if you attach one | Up to 5 MB, restricted to application/pdf, image/gif, image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp. The type is verified from the file's contents. **The file's name, type and size are recorded and the file itself is not kept or opened** — nothing reads your attachment, by design |
| A confidence score and the sources behind each answer | Automatically, with each answer | So the business can tell which of its answers are weak |

The assistant does not ask for, and does not need, identity documents, payment card
details, health information or anything else sensitive. Please do not send them.

## 3. Why we are allowed to process it

- **Answering your question** — the business's legitimate interest in supporting its
  own customers, or your request before entering into a contract.
- **Following up when you ask for a person** — your consent, given by leaving your
  contact details, or steps taken at your request.
- **Keeping the service secure and working** — the business's legitimate interest in
  preventing abuse.

[[FILL: legal_basis_review]] — confirm the basis for your own jurisdiction and
sector before publishing.

## 4. How long it is kept

The business sets a retention period for conversations: **90 days** by
default, configurable between 1 and 730. A job runs daily at
03:15 (UTC) and deletes conversations that are finished —
`closed` or `handed_over` — once they have passed that
window, which is measured from the conversation's last activity, so a live conversation is never deleted however old it is. A conversation still in progress is never
deleted.

Deleting a conversation deletes its messages, its ratings and comments, its handover
record and its attachment metadata with it.

## 5. Who else sees it

The assistant needs a language model to compose an answer, so your messages are sent
to the model providers listed first below. The hosting provider holds the stored data
but does not compose answers. These are the only parties that receive the content of a
conversation.

| Sub-processor | Purpose | Personal data it receives | Location |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ollama Cloud | Prompt completion and handover summarisation | The visitor's messages, the conversation's recent history, retrieved knowledge-base passages, the business's bot instructions, and — for a handover summary — the compiled transcript including the visitor's name, email address and page URL when they supplied them. | Per the provider's own terms; confirm and record the processing region before publishing. |
| DeepSeek | Prompt completion and handover summarisation | The visitor's messages, the conversation's recent history, retrieved knowledge-base passages, the business's bot instructions, and — for a handover summary — the compiled transcript including the visitor's name, email address and page URL when they supplied them. | Per the provider's own terms; confirm and record the processing region before publishing. |
| [[FILL: hosting_sub_processor]] | Infrastructure hosting: the servers that hold the database and the stored conversations | All of the above, as stored data — not as prompts | — |

- **Ollama Cloud terms:** [[FILL: provider_terms_ollama_cloud]] — the provider's data-processing terms, retention statement and processing region, recorded here.
- **DeepSeek terms:** [[FILL: provider_terms_deepseek]] — the provider's data-processing terms, retention statement and processing region, recorded here.

What is sent for an ordinary question: your message, up to the last
6 messages of the conversation, and up to 2000
characters from each of the business's own knowledge-base passages retrieved for it.
The business's bot instructions are sent too, because they tell the model how to
answer. For a handover summary it is the compiled transcript, including your name,
email address and the page address where you supplied them.

The business's own uploaded documents are indexed by an embedding model that runs
inside the platform, not at a third party.

## 6. Where it is processed

The platform's servers are located in [[FILL: hosting_location]]. A model provider may
process a prompt outside the EU; where it does, the transfer is covered by that
provider's own safeguards, as recorded in the table above. This is disclosed rather
than claimed away.

## 7. What you can ask for

- **A copy** of everything held about a conversation, including the transcript, every
  message, every rating, the handover record and your identifiers, as a text or JSON
  file.
- **Deletion** of a conversation and the identifiers attached to it. This is
  immediate and does not wait for the retention period to expire.
- **Correction** of your name or email address, by asking the business.
- **Objection or restriction**, and **withdrawal of consent** for the follow-up
  contact, at any time.

Ask the business at [[FILL: business_contact]]. The business can produce the copy
itself from its dashboard; deletion is performed by the platform operator on the
business's instruction, using the erasure operation the software provides. The
business does not have to ask the model providers, and neither does the visitor.

One limit, stated rather than hidden: the platform keeps an append-only audit log of
account and administrative actions, which records that a conversation was erased —
counts and the conversation identifier, never your name, address or the pages you
visited. That record exists to prove the erasure happened and is not deleted.

## 8. Cookies and storage on your device

Before you open the chat: nothing. No cookie, no local storage entry, nothing read or
written. This is audited in a real browser as part of the release process.

After you open the chat, two session-scoped values are written, and both are gone when
the tab closes: a random conversation identifier (`eva_conversation`) and the random
visitor identifier (`eva_visitor`). Neither is a tracking cookie and neither is shared
with anyone.

If you choose to be recognised on your next visit, one durable marker
(`eva_visitor_durable`) is stored in your browser's local storage, and only after you
opt in. You can clear it at any time by clearing site data.

The dashboard used by the business's own staff sets a login cookie
(`eva_session`). It is not present on the business's public site.

## 9. Automated answers

The assistant is an AI system and says so in the chat window. Its answers are drawn
only from the business's published information; when it cannot find a confident answer
it says so and offers to pass the question to a person. It cannot take actions — no
refunds, no order changes, no emails sent on your behalf. You can ask for a human at
any point.

## 10. Complaints

If you are unhappy with how your information was handled, tell the business first at
[[FILL: business_contact]]. You also have the right to complain to a data protection
supervisory authority, in the country where you live or work or where the business is
established.

## 11. Changes

[[FILL: effective_date]] — the date this notice takes effect. Material changes are
announced on this page before they apply.
